title: Swift for iOS Interviews
description: Swift semantics, algorithms, concurrency, SwiftUI, and production iOS judgment.

courses.title: Swift for iOS Interviews
courses.description: Swift semantics, algorithms, concurrency, SwiftUI, and production iOS judgment.

chapters.title: 1 · Swift semantics
chapters.summary: Trace values, optionals, protocols, and ownership.

lessons.title: Values and absence
lessons.explanation: Make a choice from the actual value semantics of Swift code.

exercises.prompt: An API field is optional, and the function cannot proceed without it. Which structure makes the failure path explicit?
options: guard let id else { throw SaveError.missingID }
exercises.explanation: guard unwraps once and exits with a meaningful error. Force unwrap crashes; an empty ID violates the contract.

exercises.prompt: A struct is copied, then one copy is changed. What should an interviewer expect?
exercises.explanation: Struct assignment has value semantics, so changing b does not mutate a.

exercises.prompt: Two variables reference the same class instance. Which statement is true after a property mutation through one alias?
options: The compiler copies Box on assignment
The mutation is rejected because a is let
exercises.explanation: Class instances are reference types. let fixes the binding, not mutable properties on the instance.

exercises.prompt: A large Array is assigned to another variable, then the second is mutated. Which behavior is intended?
options: Arrays become reference types above a size threshold
The arrays have independent values; storage may be shared until mutation
exercises.explanation: Swift arrays have value semantics with copy-on-write storage optimization.

exercises.prompt: A nullable price must become a formatted label only when present. Which expression preserves nil?
exercises.explanation: Optional.map transforms a present value and leaves nil untouched; forcing or defaulting changes the meaning.

exercises.prompt: A view controller owns a callback stored in a service, and the callback captures the controller strongly. What can result?
options: Automatic collection at the end of the call
A retain cycle if the controller also retains the service
exercises.explanation: ARC cannot release a strong reference cycle; capture weakly when the callback must not extend the owner lifetime.

exercises.prompt: A request state needs either rows or an error, but never both. Which shape encodes this?
options: enum LoadState { case loading, loaded([Row]), failed(Error) }
Two optional properties and two Boolean flags
exercises.explanation: Associated enum values carry data only for the relevant state and make impossible combinations harder to express.

exercises.prompt: Fill the keyword that unwraps and requires an exit on nil.
exercises.template: ____1 let token = response.token else { throw AuthError.missingToken }
exercises.explanation: guard requires the else branch to leave scope, leaving token available afterward.

lessons.title: Protocols and identity
lessons.explanation: Choose abstractions without losing type or lifetime safety.

exercises.prompt: Two model values should compare by their IDs and names in a test. Which protocol expresses this value comparison?
exercises.explanation: Equatable defines ==. Identifiable provides identity for collections and UI, not value equality by itself.

exercises.prompt: A type is used as a Dictionary key. Which rule must its hash obey?
options: Equal values must have equal hash values
Unequal values must have equal hashes
Hashes cannot change between app launches
Hash values must be unique for every instance
exercises.explanation: Hashable requires equal values to hash equally; collisions between unequal values remain possible.

exercises.prompt: A function accepts any object conforming to a simple Logger protocol and only calls log. Which parameter is appropriate in modern Swift?
options: some Logger when multiple unrelated conforming values must share one variable
exercises.explanation: any Logger is an existential that can hold different conformers. some Logger preserves one underlying type per declaration.

exercises.prompt: A helper returns the same concrete Repository subtype passed in. Which signature preserves that relationship?
options: func identity<T: Repository>(_ value: T) -> T
func identity(_ value: any Repository) -> any Repository
exercises.explanation: A generic T relates input and output types so callers retain subtype information.

exercises.prompt: A delayed network callback may execute after its owning screen is released. Which capture is safer?
exercises.explanation: weak self becomes nil if the screen has gone away; unowned assumes it is still alive and can trap.

exercises.prompt: A public library API returns an internal type. Why is that a problem?
options: Clients cannot name the internal type, so the public declaration is invalid
exercises.explanation: A public interface cannot expose a less accessible type.

exercises.prompt: A mutable reference model is shared by two screens. What reduces surprise when one screen edits it?
options: Assume let makes the object immutable
Hide the edit behind a random delay
Use a clear owner and immutable snapshots or explicit change notifications
exercises.explanation: Shared references need ownership and observation rules; a fixed binding alone does not prevent mutation.

exercises.prompt: Fill the conversion that makes malformed numeric text nil without trapping.
exercises.explanation: Int(text) returns Int? and naturally represents a parse failure as nil.

chapters.title: 2 · Collections and algorithms
chapters.summary: Prove complexity and account for Unicode and boundaries.

lessons.title: Hashing and strings
lessons.explanation: Choose data structures that match the constraints.

exercises.prompt: Keep the first occurrence of each event ID in arrival order. Which design is expected O(n)?
options: Track Set<String> membership while appending unseen events
Run a nested scan for each event
Use only Array.contains on the output
exercises.explanation: A Set makes expected membership constant time; a single pass retains original order.

exercises.prompt: Count each status in a large array. What is the expected space complexity in terms of distinct statuses k?
exercises.explanation: A Dictionary keeps one counter per distinct key; processing is expected O(n) time.

exercises.prompt: Why is text[3] not a valid way to access the fourth Character of a Swift String?
options: String indices account for variable-width Unicode and are not integer offsets
exercises.explanation: Swift String indexing follows grapheme clusters, whose storage size varies. Walk indices or materialize an Array when repeated random access is needed.

exercises.prompt: A loop repeatedly calls string.index(string.startIndex, offsetBy: i) for increasing i. What risk does this add?
options: Repeated traversal can make the whole loop quadratic
exercises.explanation: Advancing from start for each i repeats earlier work. Maintain an index while iterating instead.

exercises.prompt: For unsorted input, return indices of two numbers adding to target. Which expected O(n) approach retains indices?
options: Store prior value to index in a Dictionary and look up target - current
Sort the original array and return sorted positions
Use a Set with no index storage
exercises.explanation: A dictionary finds the complement while preserving original indices; add after checking to avoid reusing the same element.

exercises.prompt: Two Int values may overflow when summed during validation. Which operator reports overflow instead of trapping?
options: Convert to Double and compare exactly
exercises.explanation: addingReportingOverflow returns the result and an overflow flag so the caller can reject invalid input.

exercises.prompt: What is the concise safe way to increment a missing count?
exercises.explanation: The default subscript supplies zero for a missing key and writes the increment back.

exercises.prompt: Fill the collection used for expected constant-time duplicate detection.
exercises.template:
var seen = ____1<String>()
for id in ids { if !seen.insert(id).inserted { report(id) } }
exercises.explanation: Set.insert reports whether the ID was newly inserted.

exercises.prompt: A sliding sum window is used to find a target. What assumption allows shrinking when the sum is too large?
exercises.explanation: With nonnegative values, removing the left element cannot raise the sum; negative numbers break that rule.

exercises.prompt: Count subarrays summing to k when negatives are allowed. What map entry must be seeded before iteration?
exercises.explanation: The empty prefix represents subarrays that begin at index zero.

exercises.prompt: Complete a lower-bound search for the first value at least target.
exercises.hiddenTests: For [1,2,2,4], target 2 returns 1; target 3 returns 3; empty array returns 0.

guided.explanation: Keep a half-open candidate interval. A qualifying mid remains possible; an undersized mid can be excluded.

exercises.explanation: Keep a half-open candidate interval. A qualifying mid remains possible; an undersized mid can be excluded.

exercises.prompt: A million values stream in and only the largest 100 are needed. Which approach uses bounded extra memory?
options: Sort all million values in memory
Keep every value in an Array
Use a Set and discard order
exercises.explanation: A size-k min-heap costs O(n log k) time and O(k) extra space.

exercises.prompt: Two timestamp-sorted arrays must be merged. What is the optimal time to output every element?
exercises.explanation: Two cursors inspect each item once, producing a sorted output in linear total time.

exercises.prompt: A recursive DFS on a chain of 200,000 nodes may fail despite O(n) time. Why?
options: Call stack depth may exhaust available stack space
exercises.explanation: A long chain creates O(n) recursion depth; an explicit stack avoids deep call frames.

exercises.prompt: Display items sorted by score without changing source state. Which operation matches that intent?
exercises.explanation: sorted returns a new Array; sort mutates the original variable.

exercises.prompt: Fill the branch for lower-bound binary search.
exercises.template: if values[mid] >= target { ____1 } else { low = mid + 1 }
exercises.explanation: Keep mid when it could be the first qualifying position.

chapters.title: 3 · Swift concurrency
chapters.summary: Handle task ownership, actor isolation, cancellation, and stale responses.

lessons.title: Tasks and cancellation
lessons.explanation: Keep asynchronous work structured and bounded.

exercises.prompt: A profile and settings request are independent but both required. Which structure runs them concurrently inside one async function?
options: async let profile = fetchProfile(); async let settings = fetchSettings(); await both
exercises.explanation: async let child tasks can run concurrently and remain bound to their parent.

exercises.prompt: A view model changes UI-observed state after a fetch. What expresses its UI isolation?
options: @MainActor on the view model or mutation boundary
exercises.explanation: MainActor isolation serializes UI state mutations on the main actor.

exercises.prompt: A task performs CPU-heavy parsing with no suspension points. How can it respond to cancellation promptly?
options: Periodically call Task.checkCancellation() or inspect Task.isCancelled
exercises.explanation: Cancellation is cooperative, so long synchronous work must check for it.

exercises.prompt: A search screen disappears while a request runs. Which design gives the request a clear owner?
options: Block the main thread until completion
Store the Task and cancel it on screen lifetime end, or use a lifecycle-bound task modifier
Always use Task.detached and forget it
Keep a global Task array forever
exercises.explanation: Task ownership determines cancellation and prevents late results from mutating a departed screen.

exercises.prompt: A task group has several child fetches and one throws. What must the parent do to get and handle that error?
options: Await results from the throwing group and handle the propagated error
Assume child errors are logged automatically
exercises.explanation: Thrown child errors surface when results are awaited; structured groups keep children within the parent lifetime.

exercises.prompt: Search A starts, then B; A responds last. Which rule keeps B on screen?
options: Always apply the last response to arrive
Cancel A or compare a generation token before applying a result
exercises.explanation: Request order and response order can differ; the visible state must correspond to the latest query.

exercises.prompt: Why avoid Task.detached for ordinary screen-owned requests?
options: It does not inherit the parent task structure and cancellation in the same way
exercises.explanation: Detached work is intentionally independent. Screen requests usually need a bounded parent lifetime.

exercises.prompt: Fill the cooperative cancellation check inside a long parse loop.
exercises.explanation: Cancellation is cooperative; checkCancellation throws when the task has been canceled.

lessons.title: Actors and races
lessons.explanation: Isolate mutable state while keeping workflows correct.

exercises.prompt: Multiple tasks mutate one in-memory cache. Which owner serializes access without a lock in every caller?
options: An actor owning the cache dictionary
A struct copied independently by every task
exercises.explanation: Actor isolation serializes access to its mutable state.

exercises.prompt: An actor reads balance, awaits a server call, then writes balance. Another actor method can run during the await. What is the risk?
options: The original balance assumption may be stale after suspension
Actors never allow interleaving across await
The actor automatically rolls back the call
The server call runs on the main thread
exercises.explanation: Actor isolation prevents simultaneous access but methods can interleave at suspension points; recheck invariants afterward.

exercises.prompt: Two account balances must change together on one device. Which design makes the invariant easiest to enforce?
options: Two detached tasks write global dictionaries
A UI Boolean prevents all races
One actor owns both balances and updates them without suspension between checks and writes
exercises.explanation: One isolated owner can check and mutate both balances as one synchronous actor operation.

exercises.prompt: A background image decode finishes. Where should the observable UIImage state assignment happen?
options: Inside a C callback with no synchronization
On whichever thread happens to finish first
On a detached task with no isolation
exercises.explanation: UI-observed state should be updated through its main-actor owner.

exercises.prompt: A canceled URLSession request throws. Which UI response is usually correct?
options: Treat cancellation as an expected stop, not a user-facing network failure
Show an alarming failure banner every time
exercises.explanation: Cancellation often means the user moved on; it should not masquerade as a service outage.

exercises.prompt: A value crosses a concurrency boundary. What does Sendable communicate?
options: It can be safely transferred between concurrency domains under Swift checking
It is persisted to disk automatically
exercises.explanation: Sendable marks values whose sharing or transfer satisfies concurrency safety requirements.

exercises.prompt: A synchronous lock is held while waiting for an async operation that needs the same lock. What is the concern?
options: The compiler always rewrites the lock
Actor isolation makes all locks harmless
The lock converts the work to a value type
The wait can deadlock; do not hold the lock across suspension
exercises.explanation: Blocking and suspension under a lock can prevent the awaited operation from progressing.

exercises.prompt: Fill the declaration that isolates mutable cache state.
exercises.explanation: An actor owns and serializes access to its mutable properties.

chapters.title: 4 · SwiftUI and UIKit
chapters.summary: Control state ownership, identity, lifecycle, and leaks.

lessons.title: SwiftUI updates
lessons.explanation: Match each state holder to its owner.

exercises.prompt: A child edits a filter selected by its parent. What should the child receive?
options: A separate @State with a copied initial value
A new view model on every body evaluation
exercises.explanation: Binding gives the child read/write access to the parent source of truth.

exercises.prompt: A disclosure row owns a temporary expanded flag. What local holder fits?
exercises.explanation: State persists across body evaluations for that view identity.

exercises.prompt: Rows reorder but each row has local state. Which ForEach ID avoids attaching state to the wrong row?
options: A newly generated UUID in body
The row title if titles can duplicate
A stable domain ID for each item
exercises.explanation: Stable identity lets SwiftUI associate row-local state with the same item after reorder.

exercises.prompt: A network request is started inside body and repeats during updates. What is a better location?
options: An animation closure that runs each frame
A task modifier keyed by request identity or a view-model action
A computed property called by body
exercises.explanation: body describes UI and may run repeatedly; effects need explicit lifetime and keys.

exercises.prompt: A model property changes but a SwiftUI view does not refresh. What should you inspect first?
options: Whether the view reads observable state owned by the correct model
Whether the device has enough disk space
Whether the model class is final
exercises.explanation: SwiftUI updates follow tracked state reads and ownership. Mutation outside that path may not invalidate the view.

exercises.prompt: A detail route must survive restoration. What is a robust navigation value?
options: A freshly generated random value per render
A stable item ID and repository lookup
exercises.explanation: Stable identifiers are small and restorable; the destination can load current content by ID.

exercises.prompt: A screen changes its explicit .id on every update. What can happen to its local state?
options: SwiftUI treats it as a new identity and resets local state
exercises.explanation: A changing identity replaces the view state container; use stable IDs for persistent state.

exercises.prompt: Fill the wrapper for a child view that edits parent-owned state.
exercises.explanation: Binding passes access to the parent source of truth rather than creating a second copy.

lessons.title: UIKit lifetime and rendering
lessons.explanation: Avoid retaining screens and blocking the main thread.

exercises.prompt: An image from an old request appears in a reused table cell. What must the cell workflow do?
options: Cancel or identify the old request and verify the cell still represents that item
exercises.explanation: Reused cells can receive late callbacks; item identity guards the assignment.

exercises.prompt: A view controller never deinitializes after dismissal. What is a useful first check?
options: Inspect strong captures from closures, delegates, and retained tasks
Force the app to garbage collect
Change every struct to a class
exercises.explanation: ARC releases only when no strong ownership path remains.

exercises.prompt: A child object stores a delegate back to its owning view controller. How is the usual cycle avoided?
options: Declare the delegate as strong let
Retain the controller in a global variable
Use an unsafe unowned reference in every case
Declare a class-bound weak delegate reference
exercises.explanation: A weak back-reference avoids child-to-owner retention while allowing callbacks while the owner exists.

exercises.prompt: Scrolling stutters while JSON decoding runs in a cell callback. What is the appropriate change?
options: Retry decoding on every layout pass
Decode off the main actor and publish finished UI data on main
Call sleep on main between rows
exercises.explanation: CPU parsing blocks animation if run on main; keep UI assignment on main after background work.

exercises.prompt: A diffable data source animates wrong cells after refresh. Which input should be checked?
options: Item identifiers remain unique and stable across snapshots
All snapshots contain the same row count
exercises.explanation: Diffable data sources use identifiers to match old and new items; unstable IDs corrupt perceived identity.

exercises.prompt: A controller registers a notification observer using a closure that captures self. What should be reviewed?
options: Observer token lifetime and capture ownership
Whether the closure returns a Bool
Whether the controller uses a struct model
exercises.explanation: The notification center may retain its observer closure; remove the token when appropriate and avoid a strong cycle.

exercises.prompt: A layout callback mutates constraints on every pass, triggering another layout pass. What is the likely result?
options: Automatic stabilization in one pass always
A layout feedback loop and dropped frames
exercises.explanation: Layout should not continuously invalidate itself with unchanged constraint mutations.

exercises.prompt: Fill the identity guard before applying an asynchronously loaded image to a reused cell.
exercises.template:
guard representedID == ____1 else { return }
imageView.image = image
exercises.explanation: A stable requested item ID ensures the result still belongs to the cell.

chapters.title: 5 · Production iOS scenarios
chapters.summary: Handle network, persistence, pagination, and recovery.

lessons.title: Data boundaries
lessons.explanation: Turn unreliable external responses into reliable local state.

exercises.prompt: An API changes its timestamp format and decoding fails. Where should the format be handled?
options: At the decoding boundary with an explicit date strategy or DTO conversion
By force casting the raw JSON
exercises.explanation: Keep external representation concerns at the boundary, then expose a stable domain model.

exercises.prompt: URLSession returns Data and an HTTP 500 response. Why must the status be checked?
options: Transport success does not imply application-level HTTP success
exercises.explanation: URLSession can complete a request and still return an error status; validate the HTTP response before decoding success.

exercises.prompt: A feed must work offline and update after sync. What should the screen observe?
options: A loading Boolean with no data state
Persisted local records as source of truth with network updates written into them
exercises.explanation: Local persistence gives immediate offline content while a separate sync path refreshes it.

exercises.prompt: A page request is retried after timeout. Which control avoids duplicate rows on success?
options: Clear all previous pages before every retry
Merge by stable item ID and track the accepted cursor
Generate a new ID for every row
exercises.explanation: Deduplicating by stable ID and committing cursor state together prevents repeated pages from duplicating content.

exercises.prompt: Saving an order and its line items must be atomic. What boundary should group the writes?
exercises.explanation: A transaction prevents partially saved orders after a crash.

exercises.prompt: A service is overloaded and many clients retry. Which policy reduces retry storms?
options: Retries only while the app is backgrounded
Bounded exponential backoff with jitter for retryable operations
exercises.explanation: Backoff reduces pressure and jitter spreads synchronized clients; retry only safe operations.

exercises.prompt: A push arrives while a conversation is already open. What should decide whether to show an in-app banner?
options: Current navigation and foreground state plus the notification payload
Always show the same banner and navigate again
exercises.explanation: Presentation depends on context; duplicate navigation can be confusing when the user already sees the conversation.

exercises.prompt: Fill the status guard before decoding an API success body.
exercises.template: guard let http = response as? HTTPURLResponse, ____1 else { throw APIError.status }
exercises.explanation: Only a success status should flow to success-body decoding.

lessons.title: Reliable workflows
lessons.explanation: Prevent stale responses and uncertain transactions from corrupting state.

exercises.prompt: A payment POST times out. What can the client safely infer?
options: A fresh POST with a new ID is guaranteed safe
The outcome is unknown until it queries or reconciles by stable operation ID
exercises.explanation: A timeout may happen after the server committed. Reconcile or retry with the same idempotency key.

exercises.prompt: An offline edit is queued and app restarts. Which identifier should survive the restart?
options: The edit operation ID used for deduplication
A new random ID for each retry
exercises.explanation: A durable operation ID lets the server and client recognize one logical edit across retries.

exercises.prompt: Refresh A starts, then B. B commits first; A returns last. What should prevent A replacing newer rows?
options: Always clear local rows before A
Compare revision or request generation before committing A
exercises.explanation: An explicit freshness rule rejects a late stale response.

exercises.prompt: A screen shows cached data while refresh fails. Which state model is most informative?
options: Keep cached content and expose refresh error separately
Replace cached content with empty success
exercises.explanation: A failed refresh does not invalidate usable local content; separate data state from sync status.

exercises.prompt: Where should a small authentication token be stored if an app uses one?
options: A source file in the app bundle
exercises.explanation: Keychain is designed for sensitive credentials; progress backups should exclude tokens.

exercises.prompt: A retry scheduler test depends on elapsed time. What makes the test deterministic?
options: Inject a clock and scheduler instead of sleeping real time
Use a random retry interval with no seed
exercises.explanation: Controllable time lets a test assert backoff behavior without flaky wall-clock waits.

exercises.prompt: Fill the key passed unchanged to a retryable charge endpoint.
exercises.template: let response = try await api.charge(order, idempotencyKey: ____1)
exercises.explanation: A stable command ID connects all retries of one logical charge.

exercises.prompt: Repair an offline mutation queue
exercises.story: A saved edit must be sent after connectivity returns. Delivery may time out after server commit. Complete each stage.

parts.hiddenTests: Given one edit with a stable operationID, store one command before scheduling its ID.

parts.hiddenTests: A confirmed response marks one command complete; an uncertain response leaves it pending for retry with the same key.
